claims.statement: Secrets are user-defined environment variables stored in three scopes — global, repository, and environment — each persisted in its own D1 table (global_secrets PK key; repo_secrets PK (repo_id, key) with mirrored repo_owner/repo_name; environment_secrets PK (environment_id, key) with ON DELETE CASCADE) and managed through routes in routes/secrets.ts and routes/environment-secrets.ts.

Precedence: repository (or environment) secrets override global secrets with the same key case-insensitively; on ad-hoc multi-repository sessions the primary repository (position 0) wins because buildSessionTargetSecretSources folds members in reverse position order so the primary merges last in mergeSecretSources.

Environment sessions receive global + environment secrets only: buildSessionTargetSecretSources returns exactly [global, environment] when environmentId is set and never calls the member-repo loader, so a key added to a repository never silently lands in an environment containing it.

RepoSecretsStore, GlobalSecretsStore, and EnvironmentSecretsStore share scope-independent plumbing in db/scoped-secrets.ts (prepareSecretsForWrite, assertScopeKeyCapacity, encryptSecretEntries, decryptSecretRows, toSecretMetadata) while each keeps its own table-specific SQL; all scopes encrypt with the same REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

Secret values are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM via Web Crypto (auth/crypto.ts): a random 96-bit IV is prepended to the ciphertext and the combined buffer is base64-encoded; encryptToken/decryptToken import the base64 key as raw AES material.

REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY and TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY are required fail-closed gates: env-validation.ts requires strict base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes for AES-256 and throws at first touch when the key is absent or malformed, so misconfigured deployments fail at session graph construction (session/components.ts) rather than at first spawn, and no path can persist a secret in plaintext.

Write-time validation rules shared by every scope: keys are uppercased and must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* within 256 chars; a write whose raw keys collide after normalization is rejected; values must be strings up to 16 KiB; total value size per scope is capped at 64 KiB; at most 50 secrets per scope; a set of reserved system keys (PYTHONUNBUFFERED, SANDBOX_ID, CONTROL_PLANE_URL, SESSION_CONFIG, PATH, HOME, and others) cannot be set as secrets.

The combined-size cap (128 KiB, MAX_COMBINED_SECRETS_BYTES) is enforced at spawn/build time, after the session-target fold, because it is only measurable on the merged payload: mergeSecretSources reports per-source byte attribution and cross-source collisions, and auditSecretsMerge throws SecretsCapExceededError in enforce mode (the default) or logs and proceeds when SECRETS_CAP_ENFORCEMENT=warn (fail-closed: only the literal 'warn' opts out).

Secret values are never exposed by the API after saving: all list endpoints return only key metadata (key, created_at, updated_at) via listSecretKeys; getDecryptedSecrets is the only plaintext path and lives inside the control-plane stores; SecretDecryptionError carries the failing key but never plaintext or ciphertext.

Environment-secret import (POST /environments/:id/secrets/import) copies ciphertext verbatim from a repository that is verified to be a current member (403 otherwise), because both scopes share REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY no decrypt/re-encrypt round-trip is needed and plaintext never transits the control plane; the response carries key names only.

UserEnvResolver is the session-side resolver that assembles a sandbox's user environment: it loads provider-auth modes from the session index, decrypts global secrets and the target's secrets, builds sources via buildSessionTargetSecretSources, merges and audits the cap (fail-hard on secret-loading failure), then prepares the managed-provider env; members with no resolvable repo id contribute nothing and legacy primary rows resolve their id through the injected resolveRepoId capability.

prepareManagedProviderEnv strips all CONTROL_PLANE_OAUTH_KEYS (OPENAI_OAUTH_* and XAI_OAUTH_* incl. the legacy refresh tokens) from the exposed env so managed OAuth material is never injected; for a provider in provider_account or legacy_scoped_oauth mode it deletes the canonical OPENAI_API_KEY/XAI_API_KEY and sets the OPENAI_OAUTH_MANAGED/XAI_OAUTH_MANAGED marker, so provider-account sessions cannot bypass the bound subscription.

For multi-repo sessions the broker set fed to prepareManagedProviderEnv is narrower than the full merge: only global and primary-repo secrets (or all sources when the session is environment-launched) count toward managed-OAuth detection, so a secondary repository's legacy OAuth token cannot mark a provider managed.

System environment variables always win over user-defined secrets: buildSandboxEnvVars starts from the user layer then overlays system vars (SANDBOX_ID, CONTROL_PLANE_URL, SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN, REPO_OWNER, REPO_NAME, serialized SESSION_CONFIG, PYTHONUNBUFFERED) and strips VNC_PASSWORD/NOVNC_PORT and boot-mode markers first, so a user secret cannot shadow control-plane values or spoof boot provenance.

The lifecycle manager resolves user env vars fresh on every spawn and every snapshot restore (getUserEnvVars) and passes them as userEnvVars in the provider create/restore config; a rejecting getUserEnvVars fails the spawn rather than booting a sandbox that silently lost secrets.

Legacy OpenAI/xAI scoped OAuth credentials live in ordinary secret scopes and are read and rotated in place by ScopedOAuthSecretsStore addressed per session through resolveSessionOAuthSecretScope (environment session -> environment scope, repo session -> repo scope, else global); refresh services fall back to the global scope when the session scope has no token and cache rotated access tokens back into the same scope.

Sandbox-side provider access is brokered, never injected as refresh material: POST /sessions/:id/provider-auth/:provider/access-token requires sandbox auth, returns 409 for api_key bindings (the sandbox already has the key), routes legacy_scoped_oauth bindings to the DO's legacy refresh handler, and brokers short-lived access through ModelProviderAccountBroker for provider-account bindings with no-store responses.

Image builds receive the same secret fold as the scope's sessions: loadScopeBuildSecrets (image-builds/scope.ts) folds global + environment for environment scopes and global + that repository for repo scopes with source labels identical to the session fold, applies the same merge/audit/combined-cap (SEcretsCap enforcement mode shared with the spawn path), and the planner passes the merged env through prepareLegacyManagedProviderEnv because image builds predate session provider-routing snapshots.

Saving an environment's secrets synchronously supersedes every live environment image before the response returns (supersedeImageBuildsForSecretsChange, fail-visible: a supersede failure returns a distinct error telling the caller to retry because the secrets are already stored) and detaches a rebuild for prebuild-enabled environments; rotating repository or global secrets does not invalidate images, and anything a setup.sh script persists to disk is captured in the image and re-served even after rotation.

Deleting an environment cascades environment_secrets rows in the same D1 batch that supersedes its live building|ready images and deletes the environment row (environments.ts delete), so secret cleanup and image retirement are atomic with the entity deletion.

Route-level contract: secret handlers require REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (500 when missing), validate the body against secretsRequestBodySchema (a string-valued record that preserves __proto__-style key names), translate SecretsValidationError to 400, and map store failures to 503; repo/environment list endpoints pair the scope's keys with a best-effort global-keys fetch.

Focused tests pin the observable behavior: db/global-secrets.test.ts and db/repo-secrets.test.ts exercise real AES-GCM round-trips over a fake D1 plus normalization, caps, and reserved-key rejection; session/user-env-resolver.test.ts pins the resolver's throw/return surface over a real SessionCoreRepository and real secret stores; env-validation.test.ts pins the fail-closed key contract; routes/environment-secrets.test.ts covers route-level CRUD, import contracts, and the image-invalidation hook.
